brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 113011 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 69% over 30s (33/108 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $5,622/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, pid 113011) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $5,622/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout is breaching SLO: 83% success over 10s vs 95% SLO, with $3,172/min at risk and a 60s degradation tolerance [BIZ-1]. The lock graph shows pid 113011 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) is the root blocker holding locks that 12 sessions wait on [DB-1]. MEM-1 records a verified pact that terminating batch_replayable_inventory restored checkout to 100% over 10s, though the Continuity Guardian previously required biz.change_calendar evidence before accepting [MEM-1].

audit.report: Checkout degraded after a blocker restarted mid-negotiation, dropping success from 92% over 15s to 69% over 30s against a 95% SLO. The root blocker was pid 113011, batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction for 4.0s, holding locks that 12 sessions waited on. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the replayable inventory job because waiting would cost about $83,958 and exceed the business's 60s degradation tolerance. The Continuity Guardian failed to produce a grounded review twice, so the matter was escalated to inventory-platform without executing any action. The business was not recovered during this negotiation; outcome was ESCALATED after 1 round in 22.7s.
audit.root_cause: batch_replayable_inventory (pid 113011) held an idle open transaction that blocked 12 checkout sessions, driving success below SLO and risking about $5,622 per minute.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, pre-approve termination of idle-in-transaction blockers during checkout SLO breaches because the job is replayable, idempotent, and resumes from checkpoints, making termination cheaper than waiting.

Monitor batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory transaction idle time and alert before it exceeds the business's 60s degradation tolerance, because waiting for its ~896s remaining runtime cost about $83,958 in checkout revenue.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian presented complete evidence (DB-1, BIZ-1, MEM-1, BIZ-3, BIZ-4) and a valid termination proposal, but the Continuity Guardian failed grounding twice and produced no counter-evidence or approval, wasting the single round and forcing escalation without execution.
follow_ups: inventory-platform to confirm whether batch_replayable_inventory (pid 113011) was terminated or still idle, and verify checkout has returned to >=95% success.
Review why the Continuity Guardian failed grounding twice and add a grounded-review timeout with auto-escalation to the workload owner.
Create a runbook for terminating idle batch_replayable_inventory transactions during checkout SLO breaches, including the 4-minute replay cost and checkpoint resume behavior.
